beer-hagolah/1:ו: Tur in the name of Maharam of Rothenburg
beer-hagolah/5:א: Rambam in chapter 1 of the Mishnah, halacha 19, and as Rava's emendation in the gemara and as Rashi explains there
beer-hagolah/7:א: Tur in the name of Shidra from Mata Mechasya
beur-hagra/1:ד: (4) or sat etc. From what he wrote in seif 5 below and not that he removed the scroll and as Tosafot cited — and do not ask below etc., and with this their difficulty is resolved:
beur-hagra/4:ב: (2) and will not bless. So the Geonim from what is written in chapter 2 of Shabbat — doubt regarding their words. And here the Rif in chapter 19 of Shabbat in the name of Rav Hai Gaon and the Rosh there, and also the Rivash siman 270 ruled that even a d'oraisa doubt one does not bless; and he explained the sugya in Shabbat there: their words are certainly something fixed from their words because of certainty he must bless, but in doubt of their words — meaning something they fixed because of doubt, such as doubt regarding tithe one need not bless, and Rava argues that since they fixed it, even if because of doubt he must bless; but other doubt, even d'oraisa, one does not bless, as the Rif and Rosh wrote in chapter 19 of Shabbat regarding milah, and Rosh in chapter Kisui HaDam regarding koy; see R' Yonah in chapter 3 of Berachot and Ran in chapter 2 of Shabbat and chapter 19 there, and Rambam chapter 6 of Laws of Sukkah and chapter 2 of Laws of Milah and Chanukah and Raavad and Maggid Mishneh there and chapter 3 of Laws of Milah and Raavad there; and as Kessef Mishneh brought Rambam's responsum and the substance of his words as above; and his proof from what is written in Sukkah chapter 4 "they sat and blessed" etc., and likewise in chapter 6 of Laws of Sukkah as above; and the reason the blessing even for Torah is d'rabbanan as written in chapter 2 of Berachot and chapter 3 there, doubt of a verse etc., since it is d'rabbanan — not required; see Rosh there in name of Behag, Raavad, scholars of Lunil, and R' Yona in chapter 3 of Berachot; the Rosh brought his words in Chullin there — he holds from Rava's view specifically because of majority etc., that in every d'oraisa doubt such as doubt regarding tithe one blesses; and likewise on Yom Tov Sheloshah Regalim; and in every doubt even not because of an enactment; and there in Kriat Shema because its essence is d'rabbanan, unlike berachot on mitzvot since the mitzvah is d'oraisa; Sukkah is different since they contradict each other as the Rif wrote there. But in Shulchan Aruch he ruled like Rif, Rambam, and Rosh as stated siman 17 and Yoreh Deah siman 29 and siman 265. Rambam in chapter 3 of Laws of Megillah and Chanukah retracted from what he wrote in the responsum — Rava argues on Abaye; and there he holds they do not disagree except that he added; therefore he holds even an enactment because of d'oraisa doubt does not require a blessing; but here, since the doubt is of their words, for all views no blessing is required; and what Raavad wrote for Rava — another doubt, even d'rabbanan one blesses — meaning something the Rabbanan fixed on doubt, as he himself wrote in chapter 6 of Sukkah and chapter 3 of Laws of Milah:
biur-halacha/2:_: Or they adjoin them — a village near a walled city that they would read on the 15th and the walled city from which they will read on the 14th [Rav Moshe] — a walled city of idolaters that has no Jews at all: a Jew who enters this city on Purim reads on the 15th. If in the walled city they read on the 14th and 15th, because of doubt the villages that are visible and adjoin read on the 14th [Beit Yosef]:
biur-halacha/7:_: He reads it etc. without a blessing — see Tur, for some rishonim hold that nowadays, since the law that villagers may advance was annulled, by itself one does not read not on the 14th in any manner:
chatam-sofer/4:_: (there in Mechaber) seif 17 Yom Tov 15. NB in Pri Chadash he ruled to forbid carrying the Megillah on Shabbat; and in Knesset HaGedolah in this siman and above siman 308 he is uncertain about this — see in Knesset HaGedolah end of siman 336. In any case it appears to me they said only when the 15th falls on Shabbat for walled cities, since there is concern for Rava's reason; but on the 13th when it falls on Shabbat, erev Purim, and it is not time for reading — permitted; see what Magen Avraham wrote above siman 34 s.k. 18. And per what Magen Avraham wrote below siman 692 s.k. 6 one should forbid also on the 13th when it falls on Shabbat. But Pri Chadash argues on that below and forbids reading it even when it falls before its time. And further requires study this below — from where do we know it applies lest one carry it if the congregation are not busy with reading; see what Ran wrote regarding milah on Shabbat: since the whole congregation are not busy we do not decree; and likewise for Megillah regarding individuals who are punished and compelled; see Chasam Sofer Orach Chayyim siman 195:
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (there seif 4) A walled city that is doubtful whether it was walled in Joshua's days or not reads on the 14th and 15th, etc. NB Mordechai in first chapter of Megillah: what they were not accustomed to read Megillah on the 14th and 15th out of doubt nowadays, etc., until "if not" there is here concern of bal tosif for its time is one, or it turns out because of walled cities, etc., and he could take them out yotzei, etc. And I asked a certain sage: behold it is explicit in Yerushalmi brought among poskim that a walled-city son cannot discharge a townson and not a townson a walled-city son who is not obligated in the matter — how did Mordechai write a walled-city son can discharge? And I answered: one can say specifically if the townson is completely exempt and likewise the walled-city son here cannot discharge one obligated in the matter; but when the townson is also obligated in the matter — at least considered obligated in the matter and can discharge even the certain one. And similar to what Kessef Mishneh wrote brought in Even HaEzer siman 44: temple — yevamah to market after he gave halitzah to yevamah since kiddushin seized her from now — out of doubt not considered shav leveil bal yavor — see there. If so here too since he is obligated out of doubt he can discharge his certain friend — therefore Mordechai wrote well: if we would fix to heed the doubt here, automatically he would be obligated out of doubt and then could discharge his certain friend and automatically would transgress bal yavor or bal tosif — and it comes out well as appeared to me, correct and plain; examine: and behold Ran wrote in name of Geonim that one reads only on the 14th and wrote two reasons: one — we follow majority of world; further — truly it is fitting to say safek d'rabbanan lehakel only if they would be completely exempt, and this is impossible — therefore read on the 14th, for mitzvah when it comes to your hand do not let it sour, etc. And behold what he wrote we follow majority of world is difficult, for it is fixed like half and half, and here there are several fixed known ones that are walled and the fixed is recognizable — therefore the main reason is the second: and behold Maggid Mishneh in chapter 1 of Laws of Megillah challenged Ran's words against each other, for here he wrote sufficient on the 14th and in chapter Erev Pesachim regarding reclining on four cups he wrote we require reclining on both; and he answered: for four cups if we say both do not require reclining — Chazal's enactment is completely uprooted — therefore both required; but for Megillah since Chazal's enactment is not completely uprooted, sufficient on the 14th — see there. And behold in this I saw to settle in chapter 4 of Pesachim daf 54b where it says: what the Tanna taught — one's doubt forbidden and one's doubt permitted — is to fix the month; Rashi explained to make two days; Tosafot challenged — behold we say end of tractate Rosh Hashanah we do not make Yom Kippur except one day; and what Tosafot answered for one who walks in desert does not seem — language "to fix month" does not imply so; therefore it appears the intent is thus: if Rashi's words to make two days — certainly wondrous from the cited Talmud; in any case intent of Talmud appears thus may it be correct: one can say specifically for Megillah or reclining, since possible to be stringent and make two days — therefore since they contradict and possible to be stringent and make two days — therefore it is that we do not make two days — must do at least one day; but where impossible to make two days in any way — again we say safek d'rabbanan lehakel and completely permitted; and this is what Talmud said intent to fix month or Yom Kippur which is Torah doubt — obligated at least one day — and this one's doubt forbidden at least one day and on Yom Tov Sheloshah Regalim one's doubt permitted on both since two days impossible as on Yom Kippur because of life as written end of chapter Rosh Hashanah — again safek d'rabbanan lehakel and completely permitted — and this one's doubt permitted; examine and it comes out well may it be correct; see Tosafot there s.v. not permitted in his portion, etc., who challenged — behold Yom Kippur too in Tosafot Yom Kippur d'oraisa and their answer is strained — see there; and in my humble opinion this will be proof for Rambam that safek d'oraisa lenient from Torah — for acharonim wrote where ischazek issura like piece from two pieces Rambam agrees from Torah; and law of bein hashemashot doubtful whether from this day or that — like piece from two pieces, and from this proven safek d'rabbanan in ischazek issura permitted — for otherwise why say on Yom Tov his portion permitted from safek d'rabbanan — behold ischazek issura; but perforce also here safek d'rabbanan lehakel. Yes true per this difficult what Talmud challenges on Shmuel and R' Yochanan from that baraita — behold here safek d'rabbanan in ischazek issura if lenient or stringent R' Meir and R' Yosi dispute in Eruvin; see acharonim Yoreh Deah siman 110 seif 1 — and if so perhaps that baraita one's doubt permitted is R' Meir who holds in d'rabbanan in ischazek issura also lenient, and Shmuel and R' Yochanan hold like R' Yosi that doubt is stringent in ischazek issura — requires study; in any case his portion is safek in ischazek issura; therefore it comes out well if Yom Kippur one's doubt permitted from power that in ischazek issura also doubt lenient — again Yom Kippur addition forbidden; nevertheless permitted to make his portion for addition like wine whose doubt is lenient — if so again can be his portion for addition; therefore it teaches Yom Kippur one's doubt forbidden from law from power safek Torah stringent from power ischazek issura — again cannot make this addition and again forbidden also addition on Yom Tov — and it comes out well may it be correct; examine:
eliyah-rabbah/7:_: [7] And they do not bless, etc. One could ask: why is there no blessing on two days as with other day-doubts on Yom Tov. And it appears to me that there the sanctity of the day causes obligation even in blessing because of doubt, and further the sanctity of festivals depends on Beit Din and they accepted it thus (Rashal and Bach); also Magen Avraham and Taz answered on this — see there. Shiyurei Knesset HaGedolah answered that here is different since we follow the majority of the world who read on the 14th — until here. And it is not precise, for Rashal and Bach's difficulty is on Tur who wrote in name of Rabbeinu Yechiel that one does not bless on two days from doubt and he does not accept this view of majority of the world. And I am more astonished at all the above great ones: on Shabbat daf 23 they challenge similarly on doubt regarding tithe that one does not bless on second day of Yom Tov though one blesses, and answer there: so they not treat it lightly — Rava said majority of amei ha'aretz tithe:
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: a) [Seif 1] Walled cities surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua ben Nun, etc. And that they tied the matter to Joshua and not Moses — because Joshua is the main conquest of Eretz Yisrael. So too Ra'em in Tosafot and likewise Meiri. In Berachot 2b and Orach Chayyim 2b: why did they tie the matter to the days of Joshua? To give honor to Eretz Yisrael that was destroyed at that time, so they would read like Shushanites and be considered as walled cities even though they are now destroyed, since they were walled in Joshua's days they read on the 15th, and it would be remembrance for Eretz Yisrael in the miracle. Rambam chapter 1 of Laws of Megillah halacha 5: the reason they divided this mitzvah into separate days and set a special day for unwalled towns and a special day for walled cities, unlike other mitzvot — Beit Yosef in name of Ran: because Jews in unwalled towns and Jews in Shushan did not rest from enemies on one day, for Persian Jews rested on the 14th and Jews in Shushan on the 15th, and each rejoiced on his day of rest with feasting and joy; therefore when they fixed Yom Tov for generations they fixed each on the day he rested and equated all walled cities to Shushan because the greater miracle was there — see there. And that we do not read Megillah nowadays on Purim on the 11th, 12th, 13th as written at the start of tractate Megillah — because they said in the gemara: R' Yehuda said: when are these days? When years are fixed and Israel dwell on their land; but nowadays since they look at it they read only in its time. Rashi: but nowadays when all these ceased and Israel scattered and messengers of Beit Din do not reach them — all await Megillah reading and say: on the 14th of Adar we read Megillah; if they remain to Adar 15 — Purim and Nisan 15 is Pesach; if they advance reading they make Pesach at end of thirty days of reading and they would eat chametz on last days of Pesach — end of his words; Beit Yosef. And so Rambam in the cited chapter: nowadays one reads only in its time, the 14th and 15th; sons of villages and towns read on the 14th and sons of walled cities on the 15th. And so Tur. And such are Shulchan Aruch's words:
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: c) There. And even if there are not ten idlers among them. So there Tosafot and Rosh: whoever was walled from the days of Joshua ben Nun — even if there are not ten idlers, read on the 15th; but Magen Avraham wrote there is another view that even in a walled city walled in Joshua's days ten idlers are required, and if not it is like a town — this is Ramban and Rashba's view — end; Beit Yosef wrote this view was not clarified before Ran; nevertheless what is now customary in Eretz Yisrael to read on the 15th even though in most places there are not ten idlers idle from work to stand in synagogue — even for that view one can justify the custom: not specifically idlers, but whoever dwells there ten people who go morning and evening to synagogue — it is as if there are ten idlers there — end. Therefore Shulchan Aruch ruled here like Tosafot and Rosh that even without ten idlers, because presumably in a walled city ten people are found who go morning and evening to synagogue:
kaf-hachayyim/5:_: e) There. And that it was walled and afterward settled, etc. And one could ask: since he said a walled city that settled and was walled at the end is judged like a village — how do walled cities from Joshua's days read on the 15th? We should fear perhaps it settled and was walled afterward. One can say gentile settlement is not settlement, and it turns out when Joshua conquered it there was a wall and it did not settle until Israel settled there, etc. But still one can question walled cities abroad — fear perhaps their settlement preceded their wall and they are as if without a wall; but one can say we follow the majority, that for the majority their wall preceded settlement, since most countries wall first and afterward settle them. Ran:
levushei-serad/3:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 2 to Maharam here, etc. — he found difficult Ran's difficulty brought in Beit Yosef: how do we read today in walled cities on the 15th — fear perhaps it settled and was walled afterward, and especially since most towns are such; therefore he innovated we require intent, etc., and most towns settled with intent to wall; but Rama's view who wrote presumably it was walled and afterward settled — requires study, for the matter is not so as in siman 401:
machatzit-hashekel/3:_: (s.k. 3) And apart from this, etc. — meaning in Tur he wrote: and likewise adjoining villages even if not visible, etc., or visible with them even if not adjoining, etc., provided they are not more than a mil distant — end. And it implies that also for visible with it one requires it not be more than a mil distant, for this "provided they are not distant" certainly refers to what he adjoined to it. And in the gemara it implies for near and not visible one requires it was not a mil distant; and if one said this "provided" that Tur wrote refers to both visible and near — then for what was "visible" mentioned, for it adds and subtracts nothing, since whether visible or not visible a mil is required; see Rabbi Leibish to settle. Therefore here in Shulchan Aruch he reversed and put the law of visible first and afterward the law of near, even though he did not write "provided," etc. If so this "provided" refers to near even though not visible with it, but visible even if very far as the Talmud plainly stated:
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (ז) Since a miracle was performed for them — that they rested on the 15th as written in the verse:
mishnah-berurah/3:_: (ח) They read on the 14th — one whose law is to read on the 15th cannot read and discharge those of the 14th on the 14th, and likewise the reverse, since he is not now obligated in the matter [Pri Chadash]; and Peri Megadim wrote b'dieved if a walled-city resident read for those of the 14th on the 14th, they fulfilled:
mishnah-berurah/7:ב: (כ) He reads it on the 13th, etc. — in assembly of ten since not in its time requires ten [and see Meiri that b'dieved even an individual fulfills; see below s.s. 692 in Mishna Berurah]. Indeed it is possible that children suffice since it is only for publicizing the miracle. See Ran who is uncertain regarding villagers who advance reading whether one must read also at night or daytime reading suffices; and plainly likewise for sailors at sea and one who travels; and from Tur's words it implies somewhat one must read also at night. And know further that leniency for villagers or sailors is only for Megillah reading, but Purim feast and mishloach manot and matanot laevyonim one fulfills only in its time:
peri-megadim/1:_: Walled cities 17. Here Ran disagrees with Beit Yosef in Yerushalmi language who said to give honor to Eretz Yisrael — Ran holds not to give honor but lest there be disgrace to Eretz Yisrael, for in Achashverosh's days they were destroyed and would be judged as unwalled without a wall; and his words have two difficulties: (1) why did they uproot walled cities of Achashverosh — fix both walled of Achashverosh like Shushan and walled of Eretz Yisrael lest there be disgrace to Eretz Yisrael, for all walled also on the 14th; and this difficulty I saw in Pri Chadash too; and per Taz's words it is fitting to give Shushan superiority since the miracle was greater, vengeance also on the 14th for Eretz Yisrael too — no difficulty (2); and Yerushalmi language to give honor to Eretz Yisrael too — no. And Ran's "lest there be disgrace" means if walled of Achashverosh on the 15th and Eretz Yisrael as unwalled — still fix all on the 14th except Shushan; and Taz's answer — no, as said; and difficulty (1) still stands. And Taz's explanation for Beit Yosef: without Shushan it is fitting to make remembrance for Eretz Yisrael on the 15th specifically; and that they did not do the reverse — walled on the 14th and unwalled on the 15th — one can say like Shushan; and nevertheless he challenges well: Shushan like whom, since nevertheless walled differ from unwalled; see amud haemek from this; Taz in Chemed Moshe wrote on Taz from gemara that said neither unwalled nor walled — see there; and in truth Taz has no main precision on this and it is not "if not" — yes one can explain neither unwalled nor walled; and from whom did he learn — if so difficulty also on walled cities; but Beit Yosef tied his words to Rashi who explained like one who did not know if walled from Joshua — meaning fitting to read both as Shulchan Aruch; so Beit Yosef challenged well: if not, know from Joshua — difficult no matter how much they did not know Shushan is different, etc.; why divide this mitzvah on the 14th and 15th; but Ran explains plainly and so Taz wrote, and Shushan they did not know — this is Rashi's explanation as we say:
peri-megadim/3:ב: (2) And here one who examines Ran will see that for near we also require considered from the city's boundaries, as eleven said: visible and near that the gemara said means considered from the city's boundaries specifically; and why mention near except that in both we require considered from the city's boundaries (matter of "considered" possibly in taxes and other things); and he was precise that it said visible with it and did not say they see it from the city, rather it is considered with it — meaning together with the walled city (no, for he did not say all near and visible to it meaning for the walled city, rather "considered" is discussed); however Ran has no proof that for near we require considered with the city; and possibly from Rava who said walled city and all adjoining to it and all visible with it and did not explain or visible with it — for the baraita needed to explain a tanna: near even if not visible, and visible even if not near; and an amora must explain more — rather Rava taught us both in our presence that also for near we require visible considered from the city's boundaries; he relied on baraita: for near we do not require they see it from the walled city. And from this it is also proved we require seeing too; understand this. And in Ran it is explained plainly they see the village from the walled city when standing in the walled city they see the village the walled city sits on the mountain; and from conclusion of his words that he concluded because they see it from the walled city — see there explained thus. But Taz per his method who explained feet of the mountain — no reason except when the village is on the mountain and also "with it" language and he did not say visible to him meaning standing in walled city and seeing village, rather visible with it meaning the village is seen together with the walled city — standing in village and seeing village and walled city together; and that the village is at mountain head as said. And Pri Chadash — and now I did not understand that view of Beit Yosef literally; nevertheless it does not seem to refer to Rashi's explanation — see there; and in Alfas annotated (even for first explanation) like Beit Yosef — see there; and in Rosh no decision. What he wrote "the city sits" — the walled city calls the city; and Ran: (the writer said he says visible with it and it is not a real verb — see Tzohar HaTevah in verbs letter Dalet; and this too is greater novelty that nevertheless it is not a real verb; and for Ran — no, for considered from city boundaries for tax etc. the village is also a verb):
peri-megadim/4:א: (1) Walled city 17. Here in Shulchan Aruch he did not explain the doubt whether doubt of law like Tiberias, or one says walled and one says not walled as Hutzal, etc. (in Be'er HaGolah letter Tzadiin Chezkiya and there it is doubt of law — walling exists, but Hutzal etc. Megillah 5:2); however Beit Yosef sided that every city with a wall deserves doubt even without acceptance; nevertheless he concluded in name of Ashkenazi book that it appears all without doubt of acceptance read on the 14th — see there; and it appears so for law; and in Pri Chadash he does not lean so. And Taz's words "they fulfill on the 14th" — I did not understand, for Pri Chadash at beginning of siman brought Yerushalmi: can a townsman discharge a walled-city resident — like all not obligated does not discharge; can a walled-city resident discharge a townsman — like all not obligated, or comes like R' Chelbo said R' Chiya Rabba: all fulfill on the 14th which is time of its reading — not explained; and it appears on R' Chiya Rabba there is no disputant that walled-city resident discharges on the 14th; and the question: since l'chatchila he was not obligated — if so since b'dieved he is obligated he reads; and therefore the question is resolved leniently like every teiku in d'rabbanan; and Pri Chadash in our Talmud implies he argues on R' Chiya Rabba who said its time is not like its time — say l'chatchila he speaks and to extend dispute — if so Tiberias and Hutzal l'chatchila read on two days and bless only on the 14th not the 15th — departed from necessity and forbidden to bless on the 15th; and no need for Taz's answer nor for his reason since reading time for majority of world as we say. And therefore we derive: walled-city resident who read on the 14th is forbidden to bless on the 15th and reads without blessing like Torah reading; and if he read for a townsman, townsman fulfilled — teiku in d'rabbanan leniently; also many poskim and from them Rashi that for villages they read towns — evidently obligated in the matter he reads since obligated in Megillah reading; and Taz's difficulty on Rashal from what is written 19th of Purim — say beracha of kiddush with sanctity of day is one, which is not so beracha of Megillah with mishloach manot — their matters are not related; and Pri Chadash's answer to this, and it is Ran's answer; and see Magen Avraham letter Dalet explained (for we hold doubt stringently):
peri-megadim/5:_: If 17 — here Rava's statement Megillah 19a has three explanations as Beit Yosef wrote and in Maggid Mishneh chapter 1 of Laws of Megillah halacha 17a: Rava — townsman who went to walled city refers per Mishnah order and from it we learn walled-city resident who went to town; and accordingly townsman to walled city: if his intent is to remain on morning of the 14th in walled city which is his reading time — his reading time is void and he reads on the 15th; and walled-city resident to town: if intent to remain morning of the 15th in town — reading time void, reads on the 14th (and the explanation townsman to walled city as Rosh wrote, and walled-city resident to town not like Rashi and not like Rosh, and matter depends on intent not on act that he will delay there in truth — for then what helps act for walled-city resident retroactively; rather depends on intent of prayer as we need say below — see there). Kessef Mishneh and Beit Yosef rejected this explanation of Rava that asks reading walled city first — see there. Second explanation Rashi: Rava — walled city to town, if intent on day of the 14th in unwalled town reads on the 14th; if intent to go before daylight reads per his place; automatically townsman who went to walled city: if intent to return to his place on the 15th reads on the 14th (being in walled city); if intent to remain morning of the 15th becomes walled and reads only on the 15th. But Rosh and Tur explained Rava on the end and on the beginning — all depends on morning of the 14th: townsman — time voided and departed, reads on the 15th; walled-city resident becomes unwalled, etc.; and Maggid Mishneh and Kessef Mishneh explained for R' Moshe z"l there like Rashi; Mechaber's words are copied from him; and one can say in Taz's words explanation of the 14th which is Rosh and Tur's explanation — he reversed his will who explained like Kessef Mishneh; and there wrote Rif also explains like Rashi; see Levush interprets Shulchan Aruch like Rosh and Tur; and Avodat Yisrael letter 11. And in Rif wrote the citation: townsman who went to walled city — Rava teaches like Rosh and Tur (and if he did not cite the word etc., Beit Yosef and Kessef Mishneh already rejected explanation one — see there); and we say at reading time for majority of world on the 14th; and so Avodat Yisrael; and in Be'er HaGolah he indicated at reading time the place he is in, not the place he left from — see amud haemek. And rejected Beit Yosef's explanation one and Kessef Mishneh; and should have rejected Tur and Rosh's explanation too as said; and see letter Vav will be explained further:
peri-megadim/6:א: (1) And was delayed. One who examines Rashi Megillah 19a s.v. except he will return on night of the 14th before dawn — he left the city — one does not read at night with them since by day he will not be there; and s.v. but etc. reads with them at night — also "will not be with them" is in his mind; why wrote does not read with them at night — should say also by day; if delayed etc. to teach us greatness even if delayed. And Rashi in Mishnah reads per his place like obligation of his place; and walled-city resident etc. — text in kaf; and walled-city resident who left before dawn reads in his place in house (yod kamutzah) — not such a difficulty incidentally by townsman said reads per his place in kaf — on the face of it in what he wrote nevertheless beforehand except he will return and was not delayed there is for Rashi and depends on act not on intent at all, for intent neither raises nor lowers; and likewise from next month but intent not to return and delayed there part of the day — all per Rashi; and main act if he remained there in walled city morning of the 14th or not; and "intent" is dispute as Maggid Mishneh wrote and did not bring Rashi's explanation except for R' Chananel's view on the 14th and 15th not like Rosh nor like Kessef Mishneh's first explanation; but in explanation "will return" they are far from each other, for Rashi depends on completion of act and thought neither raises nor lowers; and for R' Chananel all depends on thought — if intent in going to return before dawn even if delayed by coercion and necessity — nothing, reads per his place; if intent to remain morning of the 14th in town even if he went before dawn reads as town; and so his words first "and was delayed" for greatness; but at end if intent not to return — not finished and delayed; and likewise Mechaber here need not that he delayed as said:
peri-megadim/6:ב: (2) And I saw Avodat Yisrael letter Chet wrote: specifically was delayed morning of the 14th — if not, even though in his mind he reads per his place; and so Maggid Mishneh and Ran; and greater than this: even if on morning of the 14th he came to walled city reads afterward on the 15th — end. Here what Kessef Mishneh in Maggid Mishneh explained that this is for Rashi and beginning of matter that he wrote "and was not delayed" proves thus as I wrote above; see Lechem Mishneh there; and "greater than this" is from Yerushalmi Pri Chadash also brought and will be explained below — see there. And for me it is not a difficulty: whoever had intent to remain part of the day even if he went before dawn must read also on the 14th in field or walled city like unwalled town of his day; and he reads also on the 15th as said:
peri-megadim/6:ג: (3) And truly Ran's view is Rashi and Rif in one method — Rava: walled-city resident to town refers, and townsman to walled city depends on the 15th. And what he wrote townsman — Mishnah's ruling, and holds Rashi and Rif hold all depends on intent; and even for Rashi he wrote further but intent to delay here and was delayed with them on the 14th — implies both are required for Rif: intent to delay and also delayed not by coercion only from intent. And here one can say therefore he said "and was delayed with them" — for otherwise this "reads with them" must be Megillah of night, for if Megillah of day and he says since in his mind he would remain there part of the day he is unwalled and even when he returned home or in field on the way reads with them on the 14th — language "with them" implies with them in the city; therefore at night; and Ran z"l already guarded from Rava's statement: obligated to read at night and repeat by day, for main obligation is by day; and so in Mishnah villages, etc.; and proof below 19b in Mishnah all night is fit for Megillah and here night reading is mentioned; and further he challenges below let it be refutation of Rava 19a from until the sun shines and in Mishnah of walled-city resident explained obligated at night — therefore explained intent to remain here and delayed, reads with her on the 14th; and forever even if not delayed — all who had intent to delay on the 14th read as city people on way or in walled city called unwalled; and he will read also on the 15th as explained in Yerushalmi. However from Rif and R' Moshe and Mechaber language "and was delayed" and they did not write even though delayed — can hint it refers to second dispute too that intent to delay is required; and below see there explained further; understand:
shaarei-teshuvah/3:_: Doubt on Yom Tov — see Beit Yosef in name of responsum of Radbaz who wrote that Hebron the holy city is plainly not walled from the days of Joshua and they read on the 14th — see there; but an ancient custom to read all the days out of doubt:
shaarei-teshuvah/7:_: Feast — Av Beit HaTefillah; see Noda B'Yehuda Orach Chayyim siman 42 who also ruled like Rif and Shulchan Aruch who ruled like Yerushalmi; and nowadays since they look at it they postpone joy one day; see in omissions Mor Uktzia who also agreed; but he wrote nevertheless mishloach manot should be on Shabbat — a matter in its time, how good; and publicizing the miracle — see there; requires study:
turei-zahav/1:א: (1) Walled cities. Ran asked: why did they divide this mitzvah into separate days and set a special day for unwalled towns unlike other mitzvot; and he answered because they did not rest equally, as Beit Yosef wrote. Beit Yosef questioned Ran's answer from the gemara's challenge "but Shushan like whom acted," etc. — behold the essence of walled cities did not act on the 15th except to resemble Shushan; and what does Rava say, etc. And in my humble opinion there is no difficulty: Beit Yosef understood the challenge "Shushan like whom" means not like walled cities and not like unwalled towns — for if like walled cities we require from Joshua's days, and Shushan they did not know if walled from Joshua's days; and not like unwalled towns who read on the 14th while Shushan on the 15th. Therefore Beit Yosef asked his difficulties; but Ran did not explain thus — rather when the questioner asked "Shushan like whom acted" he was truly challenged also on walled cities who depend on Shushan; but he asked: and Shushan itself on what does it depend, meaning like whom did they learn to act on the 15th — from this automatically difficulty on walled cities who depend on Shushan. And Rava's answer: since the miracle of the killing was on the 14th and they rested on the 15th — therefore they fixed there on the 15th; and if so when there is distinction between Shushan and unwalled towns, it is reasonable to liken all walled cities to Shushan and unwalled towns to other towns of that era; except it was fitting to distinguish walled cities of Achashverosh at the time of the miracle, but Eretz Yisrael was apart from the obligation of reading as walled cities and they wished not to disgrace Eretz Yisrael that was destroyed in those days and to include them with Shushan where the greater miracle was, and fitting to give Eretz Yisrael every superiority possible; therefore it depends on walled from Joshua — automatically Eretz Yisrael has Shushan's superiority, and from this follows the division of walled to unwalled. And what Beit Yosef wrote in name of Rambam: why tied to Joshua's days to give honor to Eretz Yisrael, etc., and remembrance for Eretz Yisrael in this miracle — end; meaning through this they will see this matter tied to the Temple and not Achashverosh as fitting, and they will ask about it and answer they do so for honor of Eretz Yisrael — as appears to me, correct explanation of Ran's words without doubt. Beit Yosef labored in vain to answer in another way and say they made remembrance of praise of Eretz Yisrael in this miracle — wondrous, for if so difficulty also on Chanukah miracle — should fix something for the miracle for Eretz Yisrael, as Ran asked initially regarding other mitzvot:
turei-zahav/1:ב: (2) But presumably it was walled. At first glance difficult from what is written siman 401, siman 691, siman 665 — and most towns are walled for residence where they build houses first and afterward wall them; and one can say there they are not strict except that there be a wall for residence, i.e. excluding a fortress whose wall is not for residence but for war; and we say most towns at first build some houses temporarily as preparation and afterward wall and afterward settle with many buildings — and it is fine "walled and afterward settled," for the first buildings were only initial preparation; and likewise here we follow the walling that precedes settlement and do not follow beginning of buildings, since main settlement is afterward — found what is written siman 401 that they first build houses means only initial preparation that came only as sign there would be a city. And what is written here that presumably it was walled and afterward settled means main settlement and fixing place is afterward; and likewise Ran's language here in Beit Yosef is precise: he wrote that through most countries they wall first and afterward settle — behold he mentioned settlement and not building houses, for settlement is the main buildings for most — clear in my humble opinion:
turei-zahav/5:ב: (2) and was delayed and did not return, etc. Rosh and Tur's method: we follow his intent when he left his place, and both actually agree: walled-city resident who went to town and intent to delay there until day of the 14th lights — and so it was, delayed there at day's beginning — obligation of town's reading falls on him and he is unwalled of his day; but if he returned to his place that was walled before the day — what he thought at first to be in town at town's reading time does not help. And townsman who went to walled city and intent to delay there at beginning of day of the 14th — and so delayed there for Rashi — does not help him to be like walled-city resident, for he sits idle there and there is no reading and nothing applies to him; therefore he must read like his town. But for Rosh and Tur also here he departed from his town's custom in wine, for at time his town's reading begins he is not there and he intended to be in walled city — therefore even if he returns to his town on the 14th he reads on the 15th, since his obligation at its beginning departed — voided entirely; and this is called walled of his day. Beit Yosef and Kessef Mishneh wrote per this method the explanation of unwalled of his day is not comparable to explanation of walled of his day — for walled of his day means he lost his town's day which is the 14th, i.e. he intended to delay there on the 14th — called walled and his townspeople's obligation departed; and unwalled of his day means he delayed in town on the 14th which is reading time of place he went — and obligation of that day's reading fell on him — end; and I did not understand his words: what difference between them, for in both we require at time of his going from his place his intent to delay in place he goes there at beginning of day of the 14th — and so it is here, each changed from his place's custom; except reason not equal: for walled-city resident the reason obligation of town fell on him on the 14th since they read then; and for townsman the reason too since he intended to delay there at beginning in walled city — automatically his place's law departed; and Rambam's words on this seif appear to accord with this: if he did not intend to return except after reading time of the 14th — automatically obligation of town's reading falls on walled-city resident and townsman departed from his reading obligation — therefore each reads with people of place he is: walled-city resident reads on the 14th per place where he is; townsman reads on the 15th in place where he is at reading time of the 14th — even if he returned home after departure he reads on the 15th; and since Rambam did not mention this explicitly it appears he holds he must delay in walled city until the 15th and read with them; and per this it settles well more "people of place where he is" — always reads with people of place: whether townsman on the 15th in walled city or walled-city resident on the 14th in town; and that he tied delay to beginning of day of the 14th after reading time per Rambam's language is difficult: why not follow night reading — if townsman's intent all night in walled city with day's beginning and so acted — automatically departed obligation of his town's night reading; and possible Rambam truly intended night reading which is whole night; and likewise difficult on Tur who wrote but if intent to stand there part of the 14th — since no intent to return to his place at obligation time of his place — departed reading of his place; and gemara did not mention Rava except intent to return on night of the 14th and did not mention part of day; and it appears Tur also intended to say sufficient here if he intended to delay there all night alone — except measure of night reading possibly measure at time of pressure all night until sunrise like Shema siman 235; and "part of the 14th" Tur cited means from dawn — requires study:
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Shulchan Aruch seif 1: and even if not walled now, etc. — in Tosafot daf 3b s.v. and the baraita is explained: per the view they did not sanctify forever — even if at end he settled it does not help; but Ran at beginning of Megillah explained: even per view they did not sanctify forever, nevertheless since they wished to give honor to Eretz Yisrael that was destroyed then — disgrace to Eretz Yisrael that towns outside the Land are walled, etc. — see there; and therefore must be they were mainly even though not walled now; and so from Rif and other poskim; requires study in Talmud regarding walled cities without ten idlers — Ramban and Rashba read on the 14th as Maggid Mishneh wrote in their name; and Beit Yosef wrote this view was not clarified before Ran; examiner will see he did not begin to reject Ramban's words; and from his words whoever lacks ten who rise early daily to synagogue should heed Ramban to read also on the 14th; nevertheless even if destroyed from ten idlers and afterward settled — judged as walled city as explained there; see Tosafot daf 3b that implies from their words s.v. as Rava: whoever did not dwell in a house until walled around — his law is as walled and did not settle; see Tur Eben that wrote to question Tosafot on this:
